page: Amazon Web Services r8i.large is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the AWS Nitro System. It features an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor based on the x86_64 architecture, providing 2 dedicated vCPUs across 1 physical core with 2 threads running at 3.9 GHz. The processor architecture incorporates 48 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a 480 MB L3 cache pool, alongside vector and matrix extensions such as AVX-512 and AMX. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of high-frequency DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz, delivering 8.0 GB of memory per core. The server contains zero GPUs, provides no bundled local storage, and operates with a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark evaluations reveal strong single-threaded CPU capability, reflected by a Geekbench single-core score of 2163.0 and high data compression throughput reaching 34.33 GB/sec in gzip and 14.25 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. Conversely, parallel execution throughput is constrained by the single physical core layout, yielding a stress-ng multi-core score of 2158.29 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 2725.0. Memory bandwidth benchmarks record uncached read throughput of 20.69 GB/sec and uncached write throughput of 17.1 GB/sec, while cached small-block reads achieve 160.37 GB/sec. In application-focused metrics, the system performs 3.8 million Redis SET operations per second and delivers 5.32 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, the r8i.large offers high memory density relative to compute allocation, granting 16 GB of DDR5 RAM without requiring higher core-count instances. The primary architectural tradeoff is limited aggregate parallel processing capability and reliance on network-attached storage across a 1 Gbps baseline interface. This server configuration is best aligned with memory-intensive workloads exhibiting modest compute demands, including distributed in-memory caches, lightweight database engines, and memory-bound batch workers.

The configuration allocates 2 dedicated vCPUs from a single physical core running at 3.9 GHz, backed by 16.0 GB of DDR5 memory clocked at 7 GHz, yielding an 8 GB per vCPU ratio. It includes no integrated local storage and operates with a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, with zero GPUs present.
